# Decisions

[Office of Records](../docs/records/README.md) › Decisions

Why the repo is the way it is, kept in two forms.
A decision record explains one larger choice: its context, the alternatives, the consequences, and the check that fails when it stops holding.
The [decision log](log.md) holds every numbered decision, one or two sentences each, with its status and the record or code that carries it.
A number of either kind is never reused, and a superseded decision stays, linked to its successor.

| [D70](log.md#d70): Proposed: restore cabin's dbx from Arch, after a preflight over every binary on the ESPs, before BitLocker and before the anti-cheat tests. | 2026-10-12 | Security › Boot trust |
| [D71](log.md#d71): Proposed: either Arch's KEK alone, so that only Arch can change db and dbx, or Arch's KEK beside Microsoft's, with Windows' opt-outs and detection. | 2026-10-12 | Security › Boot trust |
| [D72](log.md#d72): Proposed: keep `PK.key` and `KEK.key` offline, and bring them back to cabin only for a db or KEK change. | 2026-10-12 | Security › Boot trust |
| [D74](log.md#d74): Proposed: Memory Integrity on cabin-win only when Vanguard's on-demand mode or FACEIT needs it, after timing games with it on and off. | 2026-10-12 | Security › Boot trust |
| [D75](log.md#d75): Proposed: BitLocker on cabin-win as the last step, with its recovery key in Proton Pass and its PCR profile checked. | 2026-10-12 | Security › Boot trust |
| [D77](log.md#d77): Proposed: Arch in WSL 2 as a clone of the Arch user layer (`form = "wsl"`), built from the repo and not copied from a disk, without `wsl --mount`. | 2026-10-12 | Platforms › WSL clone |

| [D82](log.md#d82): Proposed: NixOS signs its boot files with its own db key. | 2026-10-12 | Platforms › Bench OSes |

| [D109](log.md#d109): Proposed: the MSVC Build Tools only if I build Windows binaries. | 2026-10-12 | Security › Software supply |
| [D111](log.md#d111): Proposed: System Informer replaces the Sysinternals tools, and Autoruns and Process Monitor get a waiver only if I use them. | 2026-10-12 | Security › Software supply |
